requirements.requirement: Route authentication and authorization messages on node1 to /var/log/auth-events.log.
requirements.summary: A persistent rsyslog rule routes both auth and authpriv facilities to the dedicated file. Direct marker tests show both facilities arriving before and after reboot, with the rule, protected file, and earlier data retained after recovery.

Direct tests show authpriv messages continuing to /var/log/secure, ordinary user messages reaching /var/log/messages, and ordinary messages staying out of the dedicated authentication log. Rsyslog and journald were active before and after the verified reboot.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-reboot behavior tests. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: it records a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot request, changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered services and persisted data, and fresh post-restart routing tests.

operational_hygiene.summary: Changes were tightly related to logging configuration, activation, behavioral testing, rotation, and the mandatory restart protocol. The only unnecessary retained mutation was /tmp/auth-events-logrotate-check.txt: it was created while validating logrotate and remained after execution rather than being removed. No failed services, package damage, or new listening endpoints were observed; socket-line differences reflect post-reboot process identifiers.
